name: Jamie Carragher

lines.why: Spat from his car at a man and his 14-year-old daughter after taunts (recorded as 'other'); not a one-off: in Jan 2002 at Highbury he threw a coin back into the Arsenal crowd, was sent off and banned three matches, got a police warning and apologised.

values_note: Retype the existing 2018 'other' entry to b06 rather than add a second line. Apology applies (60%). Spitting is common assault in UK law but no charge was brought, so a reviewer could keep it as 'other'.

name: Ian Wright

lines.why: Sent off in the dressing room after Kilmarnock 1-1 Celtic (23 Jan 2000) for manhandling fourth official Willie Young in the tunnel. In his column he admitted pushing back. The SFA disrepute charge was reportedly dropped when he moved to Burnley.

values_note: Part of a pattern with officials. In 1999 he damaged referee Rob Harris's dressing room after a red card for West Ham v Leeds (FA ban and fine). That incident is UNVERIFIED: no source found in this pass, so recheck before relying on it. If the SFA charge counts as dropped, the 30% factor applies. This could also be judged ordinary indiscipline rather than violence; the confidence reflects that.

name: Giacinto Facchetti

lines.why: The FIGC prosecutor Palazzi's 2011 Calciopoli report judged Facchetti, then Inter president, guilty of sporting fraud over contacts with referee designators. He had died in 2006, the case was time-barred and no sanction followed (currently recorded as 'other').

values_note: Retype the existing 'other' entry rather than add a second line. He was never charged or able to respond, so treat it as an unproven allegation (30%). Sources disagree on whether the article was 1 or 6.
